About the Role

As our Senior Partner Manager DACH, you'll own and grow Tellent's partner ecosystem across the DACH market. You'll inherit an established network of reseller and referral partners, including a group of key strategic partners with significant growth potential — and your role is to turn that foundation into a stronger, more predictable source of pipeline and revenue.

You'll build trusted relationships with key partners, create joint growth plans, identify whitespace opportunities across their customer base, and hold partners accountable for execution. At the same time, you'll identify and recruit new high-potential partners, particularly within the HR ecosystem. This is a senior individual contributor role: you'll operate with significant ownership, treating the DACH partner business almost like your own business and bringing a clear point of view on where the market can grow.

You will report to the VP Partnerships.

Your 12-Month Journey

  • During the first 3 months: You build a strong understanding of the DACH partner ecosystem, establish relationships with key partners and Sales stakeholders, and define a clear plan for where to focus your time and investment.

  • Within 6 months: You're independently managing the partner portfolio, driving joint business plans with key partners, generating quality pipeline, and identifying new partner opportunities.

  • After 1 year: You're driving predictable partner-sourced pipeline and revenue across DACH, growing the strategic partner portfolio, and expanding the ecosystem with new partners that contribute meaningful business.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Strategic Partner Management: Own and grow Tellent's most impactful DACH partner relationships, building long-term relationships and joint business plans focused on mutual growth.

  • Partner Performance: Monitor partner health, pipeline and revenue performance, identify risks early, and hold partners accountable to agreed activities and results.

  • Commercial Growth: Generate partner-sourced pipeline and revenue, improve opportunity quality and conversion, and ensure strong collaboration with Sales throughout the deal cycle.

  • Account & Whitespace Planning: Work side by side with strategic partners to analyse their customer base, identify whitespace opportunities and build plans to generate new business together.

  • Partner Acquisition: Identify, qualify and recruit high-potential new partners, particularly across the HR ecosystem, assessing them based on strategic fit and revenue potential.

  • Activation & Enablement: Ensure new and existing partners are effectively enabled on Tellent, our products, ICP and sales approach, and turn partnerships into active commercial relationships.

  • Market Development: Bring a strong point of view on the DACH market, identifying opportunities beyond the existing partner ecosystem and translating ideas into concrete execution.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with Sales, particularly the DACH Sales team, as well as Marketing and other Partnerships colleagues to improve deal execution, campaigns, enablement and pipeline quality.

  • Operational Excellence: Identify recurring friction in the partner GTM motion and contribute to improving playbooks, cadences, partner planning and ways of working across the wider Partnerships team.

What You Bring

  • Partnership Experience: Several years of experience in a partner, channel or business development role, with a proven track record of building and growing strategic partner relationships.

  • DACH Market Expertise: Strong understanding of the German market and ideally an established network of relevant DACH partners.

  • SaaS Experience: Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally within HR tech or an adjacent mid-market/SMB environment.

  • Commercial Skill: Strong understanding of pipeline generation, forecasting, partner planning and commercial performance, with experience in reseller and/or referral models.

  • Strategic Thinking: Able to assess a partner portfolio, identify where the biggest opportunities are, and make clear decisions about where to invest time and resources.

  • Execution: You don't just have ideas — you turn them into structured plans, actions and measurable results.

  • Entrepreneurial Mindset: You take ownership of the DACH partner business as if it were your own, proactively looking for opportunities and challenging existing assumptions.

  • Relationship Building: Strong at building trusted relationships while also being comfortable setting expectations, challenging partners and addressing underperformance.

  • Self-Management: Highly organised and able to manage a broad portfolio, prioritising time effectively across partners, Sales and new opportunities.

  • Communication: Professional fluency in German and English, comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders and operating across cross-functional teams.

  • Travel: Comfortable travelling regularly across Germany to build and maintain strong in-person partner relationships.

What We Offer

  • Flexible working in the Cologne area as we continue building our local team presence

  • Diverse and international team environment

  • €1,500 annual learning budget

  • Pension scheme & wellness/fitness benefits

  • Country-specific holiday policies apply

  • Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year

  • Apple MacBook and all the tools you need to succeed

  • Home office budget and allowance

Tellent is a leading Talent Management Suite designed to empower HR & People teams across the entire employee journey. Our all-in-one platform combines an Applicant Tracking System (Tellent Recruitee), an intuitive HRIS (Tellent HR), and powerful Performance Management software (Tellent Grow).

With 250+ team members globally, 7,000+ customers in 100+ countries, and a growing ecosystem of 500+ partners, we help organizations attract, grow, and retain top talent — and we’re just getting started.

postings.description:
As a Mid-Market Customer Success Manager for the DACH market, you will manage, grow, and retain a portfolio of dynamic clients to drive product adoption, satisfaction, and Net Revenue Retention (NRR). This role demands a deep understanding of customer needs and scalable success strategies to foster a strong client community. You will proactively uncover upsell opportunities alongside Account Managers to drive revenue, while optimizing self-service resources, user groups, and events for best-practice sharing. Collaborating closely with operations, you will refine CS processes and tools for maximum efficiency. Finally, you will analyze customer data to provide actionable insights, share critical feedback with product teams, and host educational workshops to continuously improve the overall customer experience.

Your First Year Journey

First 3 Months You will focus on learning Tellent’s products, customer base, and scalable CS strategies. Through onboarding sessions, training on engagement techniques, and hands-on participation in customer interactions, you will build a strong foundation. By the end of this period, you will be comfortable using CS tools and contributing to small-scale initiatives like webinars and customer workshops.

After 6 Months You will independently manage your portfolio, executing scalable initiatives to drive product adoption and customer satisfaction. You will actively lead webinars, community engagement events, and improve self-service resources. You will also collaborate with AMs on renewals and upsell opportunities while refining customer engagement processes.

After 12 Months You will have a measurable impact on customer satisfaction, churn prevention, and NRR. You will be fully embedded in scalable customer success initiatives, fostering strong customer communities, and optimizing processes. With a proven track record in driving value, you will be well-positioned for growth and professional development.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Hybrid Engagement Strategy: Manage and retain a dedicated portfolio using both 1:1 consultative deep dives and scalable 1-to-many initiatives.

  • Digital Customer Journey Design: Design, execute, and continuously improve the digital journey for mid-market customers, ensuring value-driven touchpoints from onboarding through renewal.

  • Scaled Program Execution: Build and run digital programs using email, in-app messaging, video, and webinars to drive product adoption at scale.

  • Data-Driven Proactivity: Analyze usage patterns and behavioral signals to prioritize outreach, identifying "silent" customers or those at risk before churn occurs.

  • Commercial Growth: Partner with Account Managers to identify, qualify, and document expansion (upsell/cross-sell) opportunities discovered during your digital campaigns or 1:1 sessions.

  • Community & Feedback: Foster a sense of community by hosting user groups and events, while relaying critical customer feedback to Product and Development teams to shape the roadmap.

What You Bring

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in German (minimum C1 level or higher) and English (minimum B2 level or higher)

  • Proven experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or Digital Marketing within a SaaS environment.

  • Ability to translate complex customer needs into automated, scalable playbooks and campaigns.

  • Exceptional 1:1 presentation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to build trust quickly with mid-market stakeholders.

  • Proficiency in using data and CS tools to measure campaign effectiveness and portfolio health.

  • A proactive, "experiment-and-learn" approach to building a new role in a fast-growing team.

KPIs & Success Metrics

  • Gross & Net Revenue Retention (GRR/NRR): Direct impact on retention and expansion within your portfolio.

  • Adoption: Improving product engagement metrics through scaled initiatives.

  • Campaign Impact: Effectiveness and conversion rates of digital programs and webinars.

  • Qualified Pipeline: Number of expansion opportunities sourced and handed over to the AM team.

What we offer

  • Hybrid working from our canal-side Amsterdam office / Cologne area as we continue building our local team presence

  • Diverse and international team environment

  • €1,500 annual learning budget

  • Pension scheme & wellness/fitness benefits

  • Country-specific holiday policies apply

  • Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year

  • Apple MacBook and all the tools you need to succeed

As our Head of Revenue Operations (RevOps), you'll bridge strategy and execution, combining strong analytical skills with commercial acumen to help leadership understand what's working, what's not, and what to do next.

Reporting to the VP Operations, you'll work with a high degree of autonomy and partner closely with the CRO (through the Chief of Staff) and the CFO. You'll lead two RevOps Managers—one focused on new business and one on expansion—and collaborate closely with the DataOps team on systems and technical implementation.

This role is built around three core strengths: business insight—turning data into meaningful recommendations; translation—connecting leadership priorities with day-to-day execution; and strategic operations—owning the metrics, cadences, and processes that drive commercial performance.

Working closely with the Chief of Staff to the CRO, you'll provide the analytical backbone behind our commercial strategy. While they drive GTM strategy and cross-functional execution, you'll ensure decisions are backed by clear insights, robust business cases, and performance tracking that keeps the organization aligned and accountable.

Your 12-month journey

  • First 3 months: Immerse yourself in the business. Understand the ARR snowball, funnel mechanics, key commercial levers, and the stakeholder landscape across new business and expansion. Build strong relationships with the CRO’s Chief of Staff, Finance leadership, and GTM team leads. Take ownership of the reporting cadence and QBR preparation. Start cross-checking numbers with the teams — get to a level of data confidence that doesn’t exist today.

  • First 6 months: Own the full operating rhythm: weekly forecast and business reviews, monthly deep-dives, quarterly business reviews. Deliver improved pipeline health tracking and ARR analysis. Present your first strategic recommendations on territory coverage, commission impact, or forecast adjustments. Be able to produce a reforecast on the fly based on your understanding of the business.

  • First 12 months: Leadership relies on your analysis to make headcount, territory, and investment decisions. You’ve built the business cases that shaped this year’s commercial strategy. If we want to grow from 15% to 20%, you’re the first person we go to for where to allocate that growth.

What you’ll be doing

  • Business insights & analytical ownership (~50% of your time): This is your primary mandate. You are the person who is kept awake at night until the numbers are clear and understood. Own the analytical layer that drives leadership decisions: ARR dynamics, cohort analysis, pipeline velocity, conversion patterns, churn drivers, NRR, GRR, CAC ratios — per dimension, per segment. You don’t just build reports; you interpret them, cross-check them with the teams, flag anomalies, and push the organization to act. When something unexpected happens — an unusual churn spike, a self-service trend shift, an expansion initiative underperforming — you’re the one who digs in and comes back with an explanation and a recommendation.

  • Operating cadence & accountability (~40% with GTM teams): Design and run the commercial operating rhythm in partnership with the Chief of Staff. Own the weekly forecast and business review cadence, monthly analysis cycles, QBRs (with the right metrics and the right view), and budget/reforecasting processes. You set the expectations, prepare the materials, track initiative efficiency (A/B testing, dashboarding), and ensure follow-through. When a reforecast is needed, you flag it and drive it.

  • Translation & strategic recommendations: You are the translator between the ground and the top. You turn field-level signals into structured insights for Ops leadership and the CRO team. You translate corporate objectives and the Ops roadmap into priorities and actions for the GTM teams. You build business cases that support key commercial decisions: commission scheme design, territory adjustments, growth allocation, capacity planning.

  • Team leadership: Lead and develop two RevOps Managers — one dedicated to new business, one to expansion. Ensure they operate with the same level of analytical rigor and business understanding you bring. Coach them to become strong business partners to the GTM leaders they support.

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work closely with the Chief of Staff to the CRO on QBR preparation, performance intelligence, and strategic initiatives. Partner with the DataOps team for system architecture, integrations, and technical builds. Collaborate with Finance on unit economics, budget tracking, and reforecasting.

  • Proven experience leading a RevOps or Business Operations function end-to-end in B2B SaaS, with direct ownership of business metrics and commercial cadences.

  • Deep understanding of recurring revenue models, ARR mechanics, and commercial finance: NRR, GRR, CAC ratios, commissions, capacity planning, unit economics.

  • Obsessive analytical rigor: you cross-check, you dig in, you don’t stop until the numbers tell a coherent story. You can produce a reforecast on the go.

  • Proven track record of producing analytical work that drives executive decisions — business cases, scenario models, strategic recommendations — not just dashboards.

  • Strong stakeholder management: you present to C-levels, challenge assumptions, and hold commercial leaders accountable. You do this through credibility and data, not authority.

  • Experience designing and running operating cadences: weekly business reviews, QBRs, forecast cycles. You know what good looks like and you enforce it.

  • Team management experience: you’ve built or led a small RevOps team and can develop people.

  • English at C2 level. Fluency in Dutch or French is a strong advantage.

  • Experience with HubSpot, Planhat, Modjo, or Qobra.

postings.title: Head of Revenue Operations

en.description:
As our Head of Revenue Operations (RevOps), you'll bridge strategy and execution, combining strong analytical skills with commercial acumen to help leadership understand what's working, what's not, and what to do next.

Reporting to the VP Operations, you'll work with a high degree of autonomy and partner closely with the CRO (through the Chief of Staff) and the CFO. You'll lead two RevOps Managers—one focused on new business and one on expansion—and collaborate closely with the DataOps team on systems and technical implementation.

This role is built around three core strengths: business insight—turning data into meaningful recommendations; translation—connecting leadership priorities with day-to-day execution; and strategic operations—owning the metrics, cadences, and processes that drive commercial performance.

Working closely with the Chief of Staff to the CRO, you'll provide the analytical backbone behind our commercial strategy. While they drive GTM strategy and cross-functional execution, you'll ensure decisions are backed by clear insights, robust business cases, and performance tracking that keeps the organization aligned and accountable.

Your 12-month journey

  • First 3 months: Immerse yourself in the business. Understand the ARR snowball, funnel mechanics, key commercial levers, and the stakeholder landscape across new business and expansion. Build strong relationships with the CRO’s Chief of Staff, Finance leadership, and GTM team leads. Take ownership of the reporting cadence and QBR preparation. Start cross-checking numbers with the teams — get to a level of data confidence that doesn’t exist today.

  • First 6 months: Own the full operating rhythm: weekly forecast and business reviews, monthly deep-dives, quarterly business reviews. Deliver improved pipeline health tracking and ARR analysis. Present your first strategic recommendations on territory coverage, commission impact, or forecast adjustments. Be able to produce a reforecast on the fly based on your understanding of the business.

  • First 12 months: Leadership relies on your analysis to make headcount, territory, and investment decisions. You’ve built the business cases that shaped this year’s commercial strategy. If we want to grow from 15% to 20%, you’re the first person we go to for where to allocate that growth.

What you’ll be doing

  • Business insights & analytical ownership (~50% of your time): This is your primary mandate. You are the person who is kept awake at night until the numbers are clear and understood. Own the analytical layer that drives leadership decisions: ARR dynamics, cohort analysis, pipeline velocity, conversion patterns, churn drivers, NRR, GRR, CAC ratios — per dimension, per segment. You don’t just build reports; you interpret them, cross-check them with the teams, flag anomalies, and push the organization to act. When something unexpected happens — an unusual churn spike, a self-service trend shift, an expansion initiative underperforming — you’re the one who digs in and comes back with an explanation and a recommendation.

  • Operating cadence & accountability (~40% with GTM teams): Design and run the commercial operating rhythm in partnership with the Chief of Staff. Own the weekly forecast and business review cadence, monthly analysis cycles, QBRs (with the right metrics and the right view), and budget/reforecasting processes. You set the expectations, prepare the materials, track initiative efficiency (A/B testing, dashboarding), and ensure follow-through. When a reforecast is needed, you flag it and drive it.

  • Translation & strategic recommendations: You are the translator between the ground and the top. You turn field-level signals into structured insights for Ops leadership and the CRO team. You translate corporate objectives and the Ops roadmap into priorities and actions for the GTM teams. You build business cases that support key commercial decisions: commission scheme design, territory adjustments, growth allocation, capacity planning.

  • Team leadership: Lead and develop two RevOps Managers — one dedicated to new business, one to expansion. Ensure they operate with the same level of analytical rigor and business understanding you bring. Coach them to become strong business partners to the GTM leaders they support.

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work closely with the Chief of Staff to the CRO on QBR preparation, performance intelligence, and strategic initiatives. Partner with the DataOps team for system architecture, integrations, and technical builds. Collaborate with Finance on unit economics, budget tracking, and reforecasting.

What you bring

We’re looking for someone who has been the #1 RevOps / Business Operations leader in a B2B SaaS company in the €50m–€100m ARR range, or a strong #2 in a larger organization (€100m–€250m ARR). You lead with business judgment and analytical depth — not systems administration.

Must-haves

  • Proven experience leading a RevOps or Business Operations function end-to-end in B2B SaaS, with direct ownership of business metrics and commercial cadences.

  • Deep understanding of recurring revenue models, ARR mechanics, and commercial finance: NRR, GRR, CAC ratios, commissions, capacity planning, unit economics.

  • Obsessive analytical rigor: you cross-check, you dig in, you don’t stop until the numbers tell a coherent story. You can produce a reforecast on the go.

  • Proven track record of producing analytical work that drives executive decisions — business cases, scenario models, strategic recommendations — not just dashboards.

  • Strong stakeholder management: you present to C-levels, challenge assumptions, and hold commercial leaders accountable. You do this through credibility and data, not authority.

  • Experience designing and running operating cadences: weekly business reviews, QBRs, forecast cycles. You know what good looks like and you enforce it.

  • Team management experience: you’ve built or led a small RevOps team and can develop people.

  • English at C2 level. Fluency in Dutch or French is a strong advantage.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with HubSpot, Planhat, Modjo, or Qobra.

  • Familiarity with BI tools (Metabase or similar) and SQL — enough to pull your own analysis autonomously.

  • Exposure to data engineering concepts (dbt, data warehousing) — enough to collaborate with a DataOps team.

  • Awareness of how AI is evolving the ops operating model.

  • Experience working across multiple European geographies (NL, FR, DE).

What we offer

  • Flexibility to work from home and from our canal side office in Amsterdam

  • A chance to shape one of the most ambitious scale-ups in Europe

  • Work in a diverse and multicultural team

  • €1,500 annual training budget plus internal training

  • Pension plan, travel reimbursement, and wellness perks

  • 28 paid holiday days + 2 additional days to relax

  • Work from anywhere for 4 weeks/year

  • Apple MacBook and tools

  • €200 home office budget

This role can be both based in Amsterdam, The Netherlands or Paris, France. Benefits can differ based on location.

About Tellent

Tellent is a Talent Management Suite that helps organizations attract, hire, manage, and grow their people. Our platform combines Applicant Tracking, HRIS, and Performance Management solutions used by 7,000+ companies across 100+ countries.

With 250+ employees across Europe, we’re building intuitive and scalable HR technology that helps companies create better employee experiences.

We use our internally developed AI tools to help streamline our recruitment process. However, technology never makes a decision. Every candidate is personally reviewed by our team. Your journey with us is guided by people, supported by tech. Curious about how it works? Read our AI Statement, check our Privacy Policy, or chat with us at hr@tellent.com.
